_comment_schema: Declared data for php-hover-scan.php's cross-file resolution job. NOT
a hardcoded if/else chain — this file is the ONLY place a shared CSS
emitter's shape is named; the scanner reads it generically. Adding a
new emitter to detect means adding a row here, never editing the
scanner's control flow.
Each key is a shared CSS-emitting function name (as it appears in
includes/*.php, NOT includes/helpers-hover-state.php itself — that
file is the guard DEFINER and is exempt from every job in this
scanner, cross-file included).
selector_param_index    (int) 0-based position of the argument that
carries a CSS SELECTOR string. Required.
guard_gate_param_index  (int) 0-based position of the argument whose
value decides whether the callee's guarded
branch runs for that selector. Required.
guard_skip_literals     (string[]) exact call-site token text (case-
insensitive) that PROVES the guarded branch
is skipped when passed at guard_gate_param_index
-- e.g. the bare PHP keyword "null", or an
explicit empty-string literal. Only single-
token, unambiguous spellings belong here --
this is a lookup table of PROOFS, not a
pattern-match guess.
EXTERNAL-GUARD RECOGNITION (added 2026-09-03). guard_gate_param_index
proves the callee's OWN guarded branch ran or didn't -- it says nothing
about a call the CALLER guards from outside, by (a) baking the layer-2
constant into the selector it hands in, and (b) wrapping the callee's
whole return value in a layer-1 wrapper. Declared under the reserved
key "__guard_recognition__" (double-underscore so it can never collide
with a real sgs_* function name):
layer1_wrapper_functions (string[]) function name(s) that wrap an
already-built rule string in the layer-1
media query (e.g. sgs_hover_media_wrap()).
layer2_selector_constant (string) the PHP constant name that proves
layer-2 zero-specificity scoping is baked
into a selector expression (e.g.
SGS_HOVER_NOT_TOUCH).
A call at a registered emitter is treated as EXTERNALLY GUARDED, and
skipped even when its own gate argument proves the callee's internal
branch is skipped, ONLY when BOTH are independently proven true at
that exact call site: the selector argument's expression (traced one
hop, same rule as selector-carries-hover) contains the constant name,
AND the call itself is the argument to a call to one of
layer1_wrapper_functions. Either alone is NOT enough and must still
flag -- see php-hover-scan.php's own docblock for why.

sgs_border_gradient_css._why: with $hover_paint literally null, sgs_border_gradient_css()'s own two sgs_hover_state_rules() calls never run, so a hover-carrying $selector reaches the function's unconditional base-rule emission ({$selector}{...} / {$selector}::before{...}) with no guard applied anywhere in the call.

sgs_block_background_layer_css._why: same shape as sgs_border_gradient_css, with the empty string as its literal skip value instead of null (its default). Included to prove the registry is genuinely reusable across more than one function, not a single hardcoded case dressed as data. Zero real call sites exist for this function at the time this registry was written (grep-confirmed), so it currently never fires -- kept here for when a future caller is added.

__guard_recognition__._why: sgs_hover_media_wrap() is the ONE declared layer-1 wrapper (its own docblock: 'For callers that receive a finished rule string from another helper... and so cannot hand over a selector/declaration pair'). SGS_HOVER_NOT_TOUCH is the ONE declared layer-2 constant. Both are read generically by Job B's external-guard check -- adding a second wrapper function later means appending to layer1_wrapper_functions here, never editing scan logic.
